units.locator: I. General Provisions
units.text: I. General Provisions
units.label: I. General Provisions

units.locator: I. General Provisions
units.text: The Spatial Development Strategy of the Russian Federation for the Period up to 2030 with a Forecast up to 2036 (hereinafter the Strategy) has been developed in accordance with the Federal Law “On Strategic Planning in the Russian Federation”, the national development goals of the Russian Federation defined by Presidential Decree of the Russian Federation of 7 May 2024 No. 309 “On the National Development Goals of the Russian Federation for the Period up to 2030 and Looking Ahead to 2036” (hereinafter the national goals), and the Fundamentals of State Policy in the Sphere of Strategic Planning in the Russian Federation, approved by Presidential Decree of the Russian Federation of 8 November 2021 No. 633 “On Approval of the Fundamentals of State Policy in the Sphere of Strategic Planning in the Russian Federation”.
units.label: I. General Provisions · “The Spatial Development Strategy of the Russian Federation for…”

units.locator: I. General Provisions
units.text: The Strategy is a strategic planning document developed as part of goal-setting on a territorial basis.
units.label: I. General Provisions · “The Strategy is a strategic planning document developed as part…”

units.locator: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals
units.text: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals
units.label: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals

units.locator: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals
units.text: The role of the Strategy in the system of strategic planning documents is determined by the need to achieve the national goals amid established trends, new challenges and opportunities for the spatial development of the Russian Federation, as well as budget constraints and rising costs in the economy.
units.label: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals · “The role of the Strategy in the system of strategic planning…”

units.locator: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals
units.text: Implementation of the Strategy will help overcome negative spatial development trends, realize new opportunities and formulate responses to new spatial development challenges, thereby contributing to the achievement of the national goals. Taking account of the national goals, target indicators for spatial development of the Russian Federation have been established as set out in Annex No. 1 (hereinafter the spatial development target indicators).
units.label: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals · “Implementation of the Strategy will help overcome negative…”

units.locator: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals
units.text: The Strategy is intended to involve spatial resources to the fullest extent in achieving the national goals, taking account of the need to use available resources efficiently. The Strategy identifies spatial priorities that make it possible to concentrate resources from budgetary and extrabudgetary sources, including through national projects and state programs, on addressing key development tasks, as well as mechanisms to ensure their efficient use.
units.label: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals · “The Strategy is intended to involve spatial resources to the…”

units.locator: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals
units.text: Spatial priorities include:
units.label: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals · “Spatial priorities include:”

units.locator: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals
units.text: a system of anchor settlements that shape the settlement, infrastructure and economic systems of the Russian Federation and ensure the development of their adjacent territories;
units.label: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals · “a system of anchor settlements that shape the settlement,…”

units.locator: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals
units.text: the main development directions for the federal districts of the Russian Federation, the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation and the new constituent entities of the Russian Federation, as well as geostrategic territories of the Russian Federation, which take account of their specific characteristics and the new challenges and opportunities for their development.
units.label: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals · “the main development directions for the federal districts of…”

units.locator: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals
units.text: Efficient use of resources will be achieved through implementation of the general and sector-specific spatial development principles enshrined in the Strategy, which provide for:
units.label: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals · “Efficient use of resources will be achieved through…”

units.locator: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals
units.text: ensuring maximum utilization of existing infrastructure facilities;
units.label: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals · “ensuring maximum utilization of existing infrastructure…”

units.locator: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals
units.text: planning the creation of new infrastructure facilities on the basis of their prioritization, taking account of an assessment of socioeconomic effects;
units.label: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals · “planning the creation of new infrastructure facilities on the…”

units.locator: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals
units.text: creating centers that provide access to education, medical care and cultural services and meet other needs of residents of several constituent entities of the Russian Federation or municipalities.
units.label: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals · “creating centers that provide access to education, medical care…”

units.locator: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals
units.text: Spatial development priorities in individual sectors must be reflected in the corresponding national projects, state programs of the Russian Federation and other strategic planning documents.
units.label: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals · “Spatial development priorities in individual sectors must be…”

units.locator: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals
units.text: Spatial development is managed in accordance with the management model for implementing the Strategy, whose key element is planning based on a system of sectoral and spatial priorities and an assessment of the effectiveness of the measures being implemented. The quality and completeness of analysis will be ensured through the creation and development of a digital platform for managing the integrated socioeconomic and spatial development of the Russian Federation (hereinafter the digital platform), which will interlink sectoral and spatial priorities and infrastructure development plans based on territorial planning documents, and monitor territorial development trends using a wide range of statistical and departmental data.
units.label: The Role of the Strategy in Achieving the National Goals · “Spatial development is managed in accordance with the…”

units.locator: Basic Concepts of the Strategy
units.text: Basic Concepts of the Strategy
units.label: Basic Concepts of the Strategy

units.locator: Basic Concepts of the Strategy
units.text: The concepts used in the Strategy have the following meanings:
units.label: Basic Concepts of the Strategy · “The concepts used in the Strategy have the following meanings:”

units.locator: Basic Concepts of the Strategy
units.text: “Geostrategic territory of the Russian Federation” means a territory within the boundaries of one or more constituent entities of the Russian Federation (parts of constituent entities of the Russian Federation) that is of substantial importance for ensuring territorial integrity and national security and whose development requires additional resources because of specific living and economic operating conditions;
units.label: Basic Concepts of the Strategy · ““Geostrategic territory of the Russian Federation” means a…”

units.locator: Basic Concepts of the Strategy
units.text: “Urban agglomeration” means a form of settlement comprising one or more urban agglomeration cores and an adjacent territory containing settlements located within no more than 1.5 hours’ travel time of an urban agglomeration core and linked by intensive economic, including labor, and social connections;
units.label: Basic Concepts of the Strategy · ““Urban agglomeration” means a form of settlement comprising one…”

units.locator: Basic Concepts of the Strategy
units.text: “Unified list of anchor settlements” means a list of anchor settlements determined pursuant to an instruction of the President of the Russian Federation and endorsed by a decision of the Presidium (Headquarters) of the Government Commission for Regional Development in the Russian Federation, used in implementing state policy to concentrate resources on a priority basis, including for the implementation of national projects, state programs, program documents and other instruments providing for financing from the federal budget and the consolidated budgets of constituent entities of the Russian Federation;
units.label: Basic Concepts of the Strategy · ““Unified list of anchor settlements” means a list of anchor…”

units.locator: Basic Concepts of the Strategy
units.text: “Small city” means a city with a population of less than 50 thousand;
units.label: Basic Concepts of the Strategy · ““Small city” means a city with a population of less than 50…”

units.locator: Basic Concepts of the Strategy
units.text: “Mineral resource center” means the territory of one or more municipalities and/or a water area within which there is a group of mineral deposits under development or planned for development and prospective areas connected by common existing and planned infrastructure and having a single point for dispatching extracted raw materials or their beneficiated products into the transport system of the Russian Federation;
units.label: Basic Concepts of the Strategy · ““Mineral resource center” means the territory of one or more…”

units.locator: Basic Concepts of the Strategy
units.text: “New experimental settlement” means a settlement being created in which new approaches are implemented in demography, housing construction, economic, scientific and technological development and other fields;
units.label: Basic Concepts of the Strategy · ““New experimental settlement” means a settlement being created…”

units.locator: Basic Concepts of the Strategy
units.text: “Anchor settlement” means a settlement whose priority development contributes to achieving the national goals and ensuring national security, including by ensuring access to education, medical care and cultural services and meeting other needs of residents of the adjacent territory;
units.label: Basic Concepts of the Strategy · ““Anchor settlement” means a settlement whose priority…”

units.locator: Basic Concepts of the Strategy
units.text: “Adjacent territory” means a territory adjoining the boundaries of an anchor settlement that includes the territory (or part of the territory) of one or more municipalities;
units.label: Basic Concepts of the Strategy · ““Adjacent territory” means a territory adjoining the boundaries…”

units.locator: Basic Concepts of the Strategy
units.text: “Take-or-pay principle” means terms of a contract for the supply of goods (performance of work or provision of services) that require the supplier (service provider, contractor) to provide the buyer (customer) with the performance specified in the contract (for example, deliver goods or provide a service) and require the buyer (customer) to pay the amount stipulated in the contract even if the buyer (customer) has not exercised the right to receive that performance;
units.label: Basic Concepts of the Strategy · ““Take-or-pay principle” means terms of a contract for the…”

units.locator: Basic Concepts of the Strategy
units.text: “Medium-sized city” means a city with a population of 50 thousand to 100 thousand;
units.label: Basic Concepts of the Strategy · ““Medium-sized city” means a city with a population of 50…”

units.locator: Basic Concepts of the Strategy
units.text: “Urban agglomeration core” means a city with a population of more than 250 thousand (except cities in Moscow Oblast). Urban agglomeration cores also include the cities of Pyatigorsk, Kislovodsk and Yessentuki in Stavropol Krai, each with a population exceeding 100 thousand and located within one hour’s travel time of one another.
units.label: Basic Concepts of the Strategy · ““Urban agglomeration core” means a city with a population of…”

units.locator: II. Analysis of Trends and Problems in the Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.text: II. Analysis of Trends and Problems in the Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.label: II. Analysis of Trends and Problems in the Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

units.locator: II. Analysis of Trends and Problems in the Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.text: The trends described in this section also determine the main problems of spatial development of the Russian Federation.
units.label: II. Analysis of Trends and Problems in the Spatial Development of the Russian Federation · “The trends described in this section also determine the main…”

units.locator: Concentration of Economic Growth in a Limited Number of Territories
units.text: Concentration of Economic Growth in a Limited Number of Territories
units.label: Concentration of Economic Growth in a Limited Number of Territories

units.locator: Concentration of Economic Growth in a Limited Number of Territories
units.text: Despite sustained growth of the economy of the Russian Federation, economic activity continues to concentrate in a limited number of constituent entities of the Russian Federation. As a result of accelerated economic growth in the 9 constituent entities of the Russian Federation that make the largest contribution to aggregate gross regional product, including the Moscow and Saint Petersburg urban agglomerations, their share of aggregate gross regional product increased from 50.2 percent in 2016 to 53.2 percent in 2022.
units.label: Concentration of Economic Growth in a Limited Number of Territories · “Despite sustained growth of the economy of the Russian…”

units.locator: Concentration of Economic Growth in a Limited Number of Territories
units.text: In addition to the capital urban agglomerations, constituent entities of the Russian Federation containing the main mineral resource centers, including the Yamalo-Nenets and Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrugs and Krasnoyarsk Krai, make a substantial contribution to the economy. Those constituent entities of the Russian Federation remain leaders in economic growth and centers of innovative development and new technologies, and also generate demand for other constituent entities of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Concentration of Economic Growth in a Limited Number of Territories · “In addition to the capital urban agglomerations, constituent…”

units.locator: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations
units.text: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations
units.label: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations

units.locator: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations
units.text: The population continues to concentrate in relatively large cities and urban agglomerations, while the share of residents of small cities, medium-sized cities and rural areas in the population of the Russian Federation declines.
units.label: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations · “The population continues to concentrate in relatively large…”

units.locator: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations
units.text: This trend is driven by uneven development of social infrastructure and other conditions affecting the standard and quality of the living environment. Large intraregional socioeconomic disparities lead to population outflows from rural settlements and small and medium-sized cities to the administrative centers of constituent entities of the Russian Federation and urban agglomerations.
units.label: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations · “This trend is driven by uneven development of social…”

units.locator: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations
units.text: The total population of cities with more than 500 thousand inhabitants is growing: during 2002–2021 it increased by 20.4 percent, from 40.1 million to 48.2 million. As a result, the share of such cities in the country’s population rose from 27.9 percent in 2002 to 32.8 percent in 2021.
units.label: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations · “The total population of cities with more than 500 thousand…”

units.locator: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations
units.text: Most of the increase occurred in cities with populations exceeding 1 million. The population of such cities grew from 27.7 million to 35.5 million, and their share in the country’s population from 19.3 to 24.1 percent. Over 20 years, Voronezh, Krasnodar and Krasnoyarsk crossed the 1 million population threshold.
units.label: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations · “Most of the increase occurred in cities with populations…”

units.locator: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations
units.text: The population of cities with between 100 thousand and 500 thousand inhabitants is declining slightly: from 2002 to 2021 (excluding the increase attributable to cities of the Republic of Crimea), it fell by 1.9 percent, from 28.7 million to 28.1 million. The share of such cities in the population of the Russian Federation declined from 19.9 to 19.5 percent, and their number from 134 cities in 2002 to 132 cities in 2021.
units.label: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations · “The population of cities with between 100 thousand and 500…”

units.locator: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations
units.text: The population of small and medium-sized cities with fewer than 100 thousand inhabitants is declining faster than the Russian average: over 20 years it fell by 7.4 percent (excluding the increase attributable to cities of the Republic of Crimea), from 27.8 million to 25.7 million. The share of small and medium-sized cities in the country’s population is also declining, from 19.3 to 17.8 percent, with the share of small cities falling from 11.6 to 11 percent and that of medium-sized cities from 7.7 to 6.8 percent.
units.label: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations · “The population of small and medium-sized cities with fewer than…”

units.locator: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations
units.text: The rural population is also declining: over 20 years it fell by 4 percent, from 38.9 million to 37.2 million, or from 26.7 to 25.3 percent of the country’s population. The largest rural population decline is in regions of the Central and Northwestern Federal Districts outside most urban agglomerations: from 2002 to 2021 the number fell by 16.9 percent, from 8.3 million to 6.9 million. Meanwhile, the rural population in the Southern and North Caucasian Federal Districts has been growing steadily, increasing by 15.5 percent over 20 years, from 9.7 million to 11.2 million.
units.label: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations · “The rural population is also declining: over 20 years it fell…”

units.locator: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations
units.text: A trend toward sustained growth is observed in cities and rural settlements within urban agglomerations, primarily the Moscow and Saint Petersburg urban agglomerations, where population growth is faster in adjacent territories, respectively Moscow and Leningrad Oblasts, partly because of lower real estate prices than in urban agglomeration cores and the development of transport systems, including suburban passenger services.
units.label: Concentration of the Population in Cities and Urban Agglomerations · “A trend toward sustained growth is observed in cities and rural…”

units.locator: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development
units.text: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development
units.label: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development

units.locator: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development
units.text: Implementation of a package of poverty reduction measures has contributed to an overall decline in income inequality: the Gini coefficient (income concentration index) for the Russian Federation fell from 0.411 to 0.405 between 2016 and 2023. Intraregional income inequality also declined in 74 constituent entities of the Russian Federation during that period. At the same time, inequality increased in 2023 compared with 2022.
units.label: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development · “Implementation of a package of poverty reduction measures has…”

units.locator: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development
units.text: Sustained economic growth is observed in the constituent entities of the Russian Federation. Over 2017–2022, the volume index of aggregate gross regional product of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation reached 112 percent of the 2016 level. The volume index of investment in fixed capital over 2017–2023 was 143.4 percent, with growth rates accelerating markedly compared with 2011–2016, when the index was 105.4 percent. Investment increased in 63 constituent entities of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development · “Sustained economic growth is observed in the constituent…”

units.locator: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development
units.text: Against the backdrop of this growth, including faster growth in leading regions, interregional disparities in gross regional product per capita are widening, from a factor of 3.7 in 2017 to 4.2 in 2022, and in investment in fixed capital per capita from a factor of 4.1 in 2017 to 4.7 in 2023.
units.label: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development · “Against the backdrop of this growth, including faster growth in…”

units.locator: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development
units.text: Trends toward concentration of economic activity are also evident in industry. In particular, from 2017 to 2023, the gap between the top 10 and bottom 10 constituent entities of the Russian Federation in industrial output widened by a factor of 1.3, and in industrial output per capita by a factor of 1.5. As a result, the share of the top 10 constituent entities of the Russian Federation rose from 53.7 to 56.9 percent, while that of the bottom 10 constituent entities of the Russian Federation fell from 0.32 to 0.25 percent.
units.label: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development · “Trends toward concentration of economic activity are also…”

units.locator: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development
units.text: Improvements in budget policy and interbudgetary relations are increasing the fiscal capacity of constituent entities of the Russian Federation. Over 2017–2023, estimated fiscal capacity after allocation of fiscal equalization grants increased in 34 constituent entities of the Russian Federation. In 2023, estimated fiscal capacity exceeded the Russian average in 19 constituent entities of the Russian Federation, compared with only 13 in 2017. Estimated fiscal capacity remains low in constituent entities of the North Caucasian Federal District, the Republic of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol. Estimated fiscal capacity is growing fastest in export-oriented regions, including Murmansk and Irkutsk Oblasts and Krasnoyarsk Krai.
units.label: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development · “Improvements in budget policy and interbudgetary relations are…”

units.locator: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development
units.text: During 2017–2022, interregional disparities in fiscal capacity after allocation of fiscal equalization grants, taking into account financial support from the federal budget in the form of earmarked interbudgetary transfers, narrowed from a factor of 2.6 in 2017 to 2.33 in 2022. By 2023, the disparity had fallen to a factor of 2.11 (disparities in various indicators are assessed using the ratio between the values for the 10 constituent entities of the Russian Federation with the highest value of the indicator and the 10 constituent entities of the Russian Federation with the lowest value of that indicator).
units.label: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development · “During 2017–2022, interregional disparities in fiscal capacity…”

units.locator: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development
units.text: The commissioning of residential buildings is growing steadily, from 544 square meters per 1000 people in 2016 to 755 square meters per 1000 people in 2023. At the same time, substantial interregional disparities persist in this indicator, exceeding a factor of 5 during 2018–2023. The least housing per 1000 people is commissioned in Far Eastern regions, and the most in Leningrad, Moscow and Tyumen Oblasts, which attract migrants.
units.label: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development · “The commissioning of residential buildings is growing steadily,…”

units.locator: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development
units.text: A decline in the rate of official liquidation of organizations between 2017 and 2023 was recorded in 78 constituent entities of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development · “A decline in the rate of official liquidation of organizations…”

units.locator: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development
units.text: Relatively high rates of official liquidation of organizations persist in constituent entities of the Russian Federation within the Northwestern Federal District, where traditional export sales chains have been disrupted.
units.label: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development · “Relatively high rates of official liquidation of organizations…”

units.locator: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development
units.text: A decline in the organization birth rate between 2017 and 2023 was recorded in 66 constituent entities of the Russian Federation. The largest increase in the organization birth rate occurred in constituent entities of the Russian Federation with sustained population growth.
units.label: Changes in Interregional Disparities in Socioeconomic Development · “A decline in the organization birth rate between 2017 and 2023…”
